title.narrative: Strengthening and Enhancing Rehabilitation, Prevention of Torture, and Accountability in Palestine

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the proposal is to strengthen and enhance prevention of torture, rehabilitation, reparation and accountability in Palestine. It will facilitate any future transitional justice endeavors.

Specific objectives:

1.    Treat and rehabilitate primary and secondary torture victims and ill-treatment, and supporting their right to redress and reparation; collect, store, and analyse data from primary and secondary torture victims to improve quality of services, identify patterns of torture, and provide evidence-based reports.

2.    Help victims of torture in detention centres realize and attain their rights as rights holders to be protected from torture and ill or inhumane treatment, by providing them with legal support and empowerment through a `Know Your Rights¿ approach.

3.    Capacity building of national actors to effectively practice their role as duty bears in respecting citizens¿ right to not be subjected to torture, but also preventing and responding to torture; as well as enhancing the knowledge, skills, and capacities of duty bearers and human rights defenders in monitoring, documenting, fighting against torture, and advocating for individuals¿ rights to be protected from torture, through legal conventions and mechanisms.

4.    Apply pressure on the Palestinian authority to implement the provisions of the UNCAT and OPCAT, specifically establishing a set of NPMs, to ensure the protection from torture, and accountability and punishment for the perpetuators of this crime.

5.    Report on torture practices and human right violations, practiced by the Palestinian government. Also, raise awareness of torture and other ill-treatment, and encourage action against human rights abuse in Palestine.

description.narrative: During this reporting period, TRC was able to increase the knowledge and awareness of human rights laws among 87 psychology and medical students in four workshops. The psychologists increased their awareness about their role as advocates and defenders of human rights, and were provided with the knowledge and tools that will empower them to put a human rights perspective into practice. As for the medical students, educating them on human rights will help them to become effective advocates for their future patients. These medical students will most likely provide healthcare to individuals who have suffered from physical and psychological consequences of torture, detention without fair trial, and cruel and inhuman treatment. By connecting healthcare and human rights, medical students have increased their knowledge on rightsbased approaches to medicine providing a moral framework that has enabled these future doctors to address injustice in healthcare in Palestine.Police officers were to be targeted during this reporting period, however, the security situation in the West Bank was deteriorating and acts of violence against Palestinians by the Israeli occupation forces and settlers on main roads and bypass roads. Therefore, the Palestinian Police Administration advised to defer the capacity building workshops to the following year. Further, Hurryyat implemented a number of visits to detention centers with the aim of guaranteeing that all prisoners have access to a lawyer. This is essential to safeguarding their rights in prison/detention centers, whether they are in pretrial detention or convicted of an offence. As well as helping prisoners prepare their defense, the right to access a lawyer helps protect detainees rights by reforming the power imbalance between detainees and Palestinian police officers; assisting the detainee in comprehending and fully exercising their human rights; acting as a deterrence against torture and other illtreatment and reducing the risk of arbitrary detention.
